$comment: draft/multiline, shared by tests/main/multiline.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. The two clients had already drifted here once — the phone honoured draft/multiline-concat and the desktop did not — which is exactly what this file is for.
$limits: The capability value carries what the server will accept. Exceeding either is not a truncated message, it is FAIL BATCH MULTILINE_MAX_BYTES and nothing delivered at all, so the client has to do the splitting.

limits.name: advertised bare — the server names no limit of its own
a value we cannot read is not a limit of zero
unknown keys are ignored rather than fatal

$splits: Lines going out, grouped into the batches they must be sent as. Byte counts are of the message content only, which is what the spec limits — UTF-8 bytes, not characters.

splits.name: too many lines, split on the line count
too many bytes, split on the byte count
counted in UTF-8 bytes, not characters
a single line over the limit goes alone rather than never
no limits advertised, nothing to split on

$concat: Coming back the other way. A part tagged draft/multiline-concat continues the one before it with no line break — it is how a sender says 'this was one long line that had to be split', and joining everything with \n instead puts breaks in the middle of their sentence.

concat.name: a concat part runs straight on
concat.text: one long line that had to be split

concat.name: concat on the first part means nothing, there is nothing before it
mixed, which is the case that gets it wrong
an empty part is a blank line, not nothing

$linelen: An IRC line is 512 bytes and that budget covers the prefix the server prepends on the way out, so what can actually be said is 512 minus ":nick!user@host PRIVMSG #channel :" and the CRLF. Over it, rIRCd answers 417 and delivers nothing — not truncated, dropped.

budget.name: the mask is known, so the budget is exact
a longer target leaves less room
no mask yet, so the server's stated maxima are assumed
a server that allows longer lines is taken at its word

$split: Cutting one over-long line into pieces that fit. Measured in UTF-8 bytes, split between whole grapheme clusters, and preferring a space so words survive. Not code points: a flag is two, a skin tone is two, and a family is seven with the joins in between — cutting between any of them leaves half an emoji at the end of one message and a stray modifier at the start of the next.

split.name: breaks at a space rather than mid-word
split.note: the space stays on the piece before it, so a concat batch rejoins to exactly what was typed

split.name: a single long word has to be cut somewhere
an empty line stays one empty line
a skin tone stays on its thumb, and the pieces still join back up
a flag is one thing, not two letters
a cluster with no space before it is still not cut in half
